assumptions: This is analysis only. No files were edited, tests run, dependencies changed, or training launched.

The supplied paper text was read through its conclusion and references. Figures are represented only by captions and surrounding prose; numerical plot data from Figs. 5–8 are unavailable in the supplied text.
Reading the canonical AGENTS.md was attempted but rejected by the execution policy. Its contents and repository-specific instructions remain unconfirmed.
The supplied design document describes the MoE-CTS base; its code, checkpoint, observation implementation, and reported measurements were not independently inspected.

The paper does not specify H1, network widths, CNN kernels, GRU hidden sizes, transformer depth/head count, latent dimensions, U-Net topology, activation functions, normalization, or parameter counts.

The paper does not specify optimizer settings, PPO hyperparameters, rollout length, simulator/control time steps, auxiliary-loss scheduling, gradient routing between modules, or total environment transitions.
The paper references domain randomization in PIE [31] without listing parameters or ranges. Those values cannot be attributed to START from this text.
The paper does not provide camera intrinsics, mounting extrinsics, depth range, simulated depth corruption parameters, filter settings, or separate module inference timings.
Any Go2 integration choices, initialization strategy, calibration procedure, and evaluation gates below are proposed engineering decisions, not reported START results.

summary:
The faithful START graft requires the full depth-to-reconstructed-map pipeline, recurrent implicit-explicit estimator with transformer fusion and VAE supervision, asymmetric PPO actor-critic, AdaSmpl, edge reward, and progressive sparse-terrain curriculum. A 187-point terrain encoder appended to the existing actor would be a reduced variant. START trains its components concurrently in one stage; it does not report a teacher-training then student-distillation recipe. The supplied text supports the detailed specification below, but does not expose exact numerical data in simulation plots or many reproduction hyperparameters. No scientific equivalence or implementation verification is claimed.

modules:
1. Observations and actor: o_t=[body angular velocity(3), robot-frame gravity(3), velocity command(3), joint positions(12), joint velocities(12), previous action(12)], totaling 45 dimensions. Actor consumes current o_t, explicit estimate e_hat_t, and implicit z_t, and outputs 12 joint-position targets. Critic receives o_t plus privileged s_t=[ground-truth base velocity, foot contact states, body heightmap H_b, four-foot heightmaps H_f]. Critic architecture and heightmap dimensions are unspecified. [§II-A.1, Eqs. (1),(2), Fig. 2]
2. I-E Estimator: a GRU processes proprioceptive history o_t^H1 into z_prop; a CNN encodes the reconstructed local heightmap into z_map. Transformer encoder layers fuse the modalities and support spatial reasoning over terrain tokens. Outputs are implicit VAE latent z_t and explicit e_hat_t=[v_hat_t,z_hat_b,z_hat_f]. Body and foot descriptors decode to H_hat_b and H_hat_f; foot-centric terrain is described as within 0.1 m. Foot-map resolution, exact shape, and whether 0.1 m denotes radius or another extent are not stated. Unlike foot-clearance prediction alone, these maps encode detailed local foot terrain. A decoder uses all estimation vectors to predict next proprioception. [§II-A.2, Fig. 2]
3. I-E loss: L_IE=KL(q(z_t|o_t^H1,H_hat_map)||p(z_t))+MSE(o_hat_(t+1),o_(t+1))+MSE(v_hat_t,v_t)+MSE(H_hat_f,H_f)+MSE(H_hat_b,H_b). Equation (3) prints unit coefficients; the prior distribution, latent sampling convention at deployment, and any additional implementation weighting are not specified. [Eq. (3)]
4. TR-Net: inputs are z_prop from the estimator and temporal depth images d_t^H2 with H2=2. A CNN extracts depth features; concatenation with z_prop feeds a recurrent GRU that remembers terrain beneath and behind the robot. An MLP decodes a rough map, then a U-Net-based refinement decoder recovers geometric detail and reduces noisy or blurry edges. Exact frame spacing, recurrent-state update rates, and U-Net connectivity are not specified. [§II-B, Fig. 3]
5. Map contract: robot-local heightmap covers x from -0.5 m to +1.1 m, width 0.8 m, resolution 0.05 m. This corresponds to 32×16 spatial intervals, but a 32×16 tensor versus endpoint-inclusive sample counts is not specified. Height datum, yaw alignment convention, clipping, missing-data encoding, and output normalization are not given. The existing 17×11, 0.1 m base scan is not this map. [§II-B; supplied design §§2–3]
6. Reconstruction loss: L_TR=MSE(H_hat_rough,H_b)+L1(H_hat_refined,H_b). Rough-map MSE supplies reconstruction supervision; refined-map L1 counters oversmoothing and improves edge and flat-surface fidelity. Both supervise privileged terrain geometry, not camera visibility alone. [§II-B, Eq. (4)]
7. AdaSmpl: substitute ground-truth maps for reconstructed maps at the policy input with p_smpl=tanh(CV(R)), where R denotes episode rewards. Higher reward variation produces more privileged-map use; stable training reduces it. Deployment uses reconstructed maps exclusively. Reward window, CV denominator stabilization, negative/zero-mean handling, sampling granularity, and whether substituted samples still train TR-Net are not specified. Faithful intent requires retaining TR-Net supervision while easing policy exploration, but exact implementation must be declared. [§II-C, Eq. (5), Fig. 3]

training:
1. One concurrent training stage combines TR-Net, supervised I-E estimation, and PPO actor learning under an asymmetric actor-critic. The paper explicitly avoids a two-stage information gap. Curriculum progression within this stage is not a separate teacher/student stage. Gradient sharing, detach points, total combined objective coefficients, and optimizer partitioning are unspecified. [§II-A, §II-D.1]
2. Reported budget: Isaac Gym, 3,072 parallel Lite3 instances, one NVIDIA RTX A6000, approximately 10,000 iterations and 16.6 hours. NVIDIA Warp renders 60×60 depth images instead of Isaac Gym's default camera interface. These are reported Lite3 training conditions, not a measured Go2 budget. [§II-D.1]
3. Termination: reset if the robot flips beyond predefined angular limits or a foot drops below a specified threshold beneath the ground plane. Neither numeric threshold is given. [§II-D.1]
4. Commands: robot-frame forward velocity uniform in [0,1.5] m/s; lateral velocity zero. Forward commands below 0.3 m/s are clamped to zero, and yaw velocity is sampled from [-1.2,1.2] rad/s when forward command is zero. The paper calls this forward walking and turning capability; its written sampling rule does not establish simultaneous nonzero forward and yaw commands. Command resampling interval and nonzero-forward yaw settings are unspecified. [§II-D.1]
5. Domain randomization follows PIE [31]. No actual randomized quantities, ranges, distributions, update frequencies, or noise/delay models are supplied. [§II-D.1]
6. No simulation depth-noise model, rendering frequency, camera field of view, invalid-pixel process, or simulated librealsense filter recipe is reported. Depth resolution and Warp rendering are the only explicit simulation depth settings. [§II-D.1]

rewards_and_curriculum:
1. Table I lists 14 rewards. Linear velocity tracking: exp(-||min(v,v_cmd)-v_cmd||²/0.25), coefficient +1.5. Angular velocity tracking: exp(-||omega_yaw-omega_yaw_cmd||²/0.25), +0.5. Vertical linear velocity v_z², -2.0. Roll/pitch angular velocity ||omega_xy||², -0.05. Orientation g_x²+g_y², -1.0. Sum squared joint torques, -1.0e-5. Action-rate sum |a_t-a_(t-1)|², -0.01. Smoothness sum |a_t-2a_(t-1)+a_(t-2)|², -0.01. Joint power sum |tau_j||qdot_j|, -2.0e-5. Joint acceleration sum |qddot_j|², -2.5e-7. Joint default-pose error sum |q_j-q_default_j|², -0.01. Collision sum over contact bodies 1{F_i>0.1}, -10.0. Stumble 1{exists i:|F_i,xy|>4|F_i,z|}, -1.0. Feet-edge contact-weighted sum over distance masks, -1.0. Exact contact-body selection, force aggregation convention, and reward time scaling are unspecified. The angular-command typography is corrupted in the supplied extraction, but its meaning is clear from the term label. [Table I]
2. Feet edge: r_feetedge=-sum_i c_i sum_d omega_d E_d[p_i], with edge-distance thresholds [2.5,5.0] cm and corresponding weights [1.0,0.5]. E_d is a boolean mask for proximity to an edge; c_i gates by foot contact. Table I expresses the positive mask sum with coefficient -1.0; Eq. (6) already includes the minus. Implement one negative contribution, avoiding a double negative. Under the stated within-distance definition, the masks overlap: a contact inside 2.5 cm contributes -1.5 and one between 2.5 and 5 cm contributes -0.5. Edge extraction and discretization conventions are unspecified. [§II-D.2, Eq. (6), Table I]
3. Four training terrain types each have 10 difficulty levels. Difficulty increases using the curriculum of [41], but promotion/demotion thresholds are not reproduced. Each patch is 8×4 m. Terrain depths are sampled from [0.2,0.7] m; stone/beam height variations reach ±0.05 m. Sparsity means non-steppable area divided by total area. [§II-D.3, Fig. 4]
4. Stepping stones reach 76.3% sparsity with 0.2 m stone width, 0.25 m x gaps, and 0.175 m y gaps. Balance beams reach 0.175 m width. Stepping beams reach 64.7% sparsity with 0.15 m width and 0.275 m gaps. Gaps reach 0.7 m, described as twice robot length. Complete per-level geometry tables and terrain proportions are not specified. [§II-D.3]
5. Terrain progression: begin sparse-terrain robots on low-randomness stepping stones with auxiliary flat terrain, then probabilistically allocate them to high-randomness stones, balance beams, and stepping beams. Gaps are excluded from this progression. The printed schedule has max/min ordering inconsistent with an increasing ramp; prose indicates a linear increase bounded by 0 and p_max. A proposed implementation is p_advance=clip(p_max*(T-T_start)/(T_end-T_start),0,p_max), explicitly identified as an interpretation of the intended schedule. Values for p_max, T_start, T_end, the definition of T, flat-ground proportion, and destination proportions are absent. [§II-D.3, Fig. 4(a)]
6. High-randomness stones: shift each stone along both axes by up to 0.5 times the gap and shift entire columns along x by up to 0.45 times the gap. Distributions and low-randomness values are not stated. [§II-D.3, Fig. 4(b)]

ablations:
1. Eight variants: HMap GT feeds ground-truth maps with other settings retained; PIE removes TR-Net and uses PIE-identical implicit 2D-GRU encoding; TR-Net w/o Prop removes proprioceptive input; w/o GRU replaces reconstruction GRU with an MLP; w/o Refine passes rough maps without U-Net; START w/o AdaSmpl always uses reconstructed maps; w/o FtEdge removes the edge reward; w/o TerProg starts directly on risky terrains. I-E estimation is not ablated because prior works [31],[37] already evaluated it. [§III-A]
2. Simulation protocol: 500 runs over a 6 m traversal on 10 randomly generated terrains. Exact run allocation across terrain instances and difficulty levels is not explicit. Success rate measures complete traversal; traversing rate measures distance before falling divided by total distance; MEV measures the fraction of steps on edges at highest difficulty. Reconstruction error is measured for TR-Net methods. [§III-A]
3. Fig. 5 compares reconstruction errors at maximum difficulty: no GRU is worst; no proprioception is only slightly better; no refinement has noisy maps and poor edge detail; full TR-Net is best. Exact errors, units, error aggregation, and numerical uncertainty are unavailable in the supplied text. [§III-B.1, Fig. 5]
4. Fig. 6 compares success and traversing rates against difficulty, plus highest-difficulty MEV, across four terrain types and both ablation groups. Exact points and MEV numbers are unavailable. Text reports degraded sparse-terrain adaptability for PIE, reduced performance without proprioception or memory, edge-related degradation without refinement, poorer sample efficiency without AdaSmpl, high MEV without FtEdge, and broadly failed learning without TerProg. These are reported qualitative findings, not independently measured values. [§III-B.2, Fig. 6]
5. Fig. 7 uses 500 runs per policy and KDE of recorded footholds for START, HMap GT, and PIE at highest-difficulty stones. START resembles HMap GT with concentrated center placement; PIE has broader, edge-shifted placement. No numerical distribution statistics are supplied. [§III-B.2, Fig. 7]
6. Fig. 8 compares episode edge reward and total reward for START, PIE, and START w/o AdaSmpl. START reportedly converges faster with better edge reward. Exact rewards, convergence iterations, sample-efficiency ratios, and uncertainty are unavailable. [§III-B.2, Fig. 8]
7. Real-world Table II: each method is tested five times. Order below is stones success/traversing, balance beams success/traversing, stepping beams success/traversing, gap success. Conditions are 76.3% stones sparsity, 0.2 m balance-beam width, 58.8% stepping-beam sparsity, and 0.7 m gaps. Gap traversing rates are not reported; the meaning of the ± dispersion is not explicitly defined in the supplied text. HMap GT is omitted because no MoCap device was available. [§III-C, Table II]

 deployment:
1. Robot is DEEP Robotics Lite3. A head-mounted Intel RealSense D435i captures raw depth at 10 Hz. librealsense decimation, temporal, and hole-filling filters produce 60×60 images. Filter ordering beyond the listed sequence, settings, resize/crop mechanism, and raw resolution are unspecified. [§III-C]
2. Onboard Jetson Orin NX runs TensorRT-accelerated inference and outputs actions at 50 Hz. TR-Net's separate update frequency, inference latency, recurrent-state timing, motor PD rate, gains, action scaling, power mode, and memory use are not reported. [§III-C]
3. Reported maximum traversal speed is 1.5 m/s. Fig. 9 describes slower, low-step-frequency centered placements on stones, and body alignment followed by a high-step-frequency inverted-triangle stance on balance beams. No numerical gait frequencies or force profiles are given. [§III-C, Fig. 9]
4. Outdoor demonstrations include grassy ramps, park benches, irregular single-column stones over water, descending stairs, vegetation occlusions, and slippery 0.15 m flowerbed edges. The paper reports zero-shot deployment and recovery from a slip on uneven stones. Outdoor trial counts and success statistics are absent. [§III-D, Fig. 10]
5. Limitations: controlled evaluation covers four representative terrain types; more varied terrain combinations remain future work. Better edge preservation and richer intermediate geometry such as voxels are proposed future directions. There is no reported quantitative study of lighting, camera dropout, moving terrain, payload variation, or long-term deployment reliability. [§IV]

faithful_graft_on_moects:
1. Scope: preserve Go2 embodiment and the E1 MoE-CTS locomotion foundation, while adding every START perception and estimation component. Label the result a START-derived MoE-CTS hybrid. The supplied design's actor-only map branch, omitted explicit heads, and inherited reward recipe are appropriate controlled variants but do not constitute the full START recipe. [supplied design §§1–3; START §II]
2. Keep: Go2 assets and calibrated dynamics; verified joint ordering, limits, action-to-target conversion, low-level control interface, deployment transport, and reusable PPO/environment infrastructure. Keep the E1 checkpoint as a baseline and candidate initialization. Keep the velocity-command interface, but explicitly choose between START's forward/turn-in-place command distribution and the base's broader x/y/yaw commands. Their difference is an experimental factor. All retained infrastructure still requires code inspection before implementation. [supplied design §§2–3; START §§II-A.1,II-D.1]
3. Perception contract: add a simulated forward D435i with measured Go2 mounting geometry and camera intrinsics; render 60×60 depth with two-frame history; reproduce the deployed filter pipeline with declared settings. Add episode-scoped recurrent state and timestamped asynchronous depth/proprioception handling. Calibrate coordinates using known planes, steps, edges, and occluded terrain before relying on reconstruction. Simulation camera noise and filter settings must be chosen and recorded because START does not supply them. [START §§II-B,II-D.1,III-C]
4. Add the full TR-Net: depth CNN plus z_prop, memory GRU, rough MLP decoder, U-Net refinement, and both Eq. (4) losses. Build privileged terrain labels over the complete 1.6×0.8 m extent at 5 cm spacing, including behind and beneath the body. Resolve sample counts and height reference explicitly. Retain the 187-point scan for legacy teacher/critic compatibility if necessary, but create a separate dense map; upsampling 187 values cannot supply missing ground-truth edge detail. Do not feed privileged geometry into the deployed actor. [START §II-B; supplied design §3]
5. Add the full I-E Estimator: proprioceptive-history GRU, reconstructed-map CNN, transformer encoder fusion, VAE implicit latent, explicit velocity/body/foot descriptors, body/foot decoders, and next-proprioception decoder. Train every term in Eq. (3). Feed current proprioception and both explicit and implicit estimates into the actor. Resolve unspecified H1, map-token scheme, dimensions, and all layer sizes as documented design assumptions rather than silently replacing the estimator with an MLP map latent. [START §II-A]
6. MoE coexistence: preserve the existing MoE computation where compatible and extend its actor conditioning with START estimates. Initializing preserved actor columns from E1 and new columns to zero can preserve the initial output only when the actual architecture permits it; that is a proposed initialization property to check later. New map-conditioning weights must remain trainable. Existing proprioceptive student/teacher distillation may be retained as an explicitly additional hybrid objective, with separate logging and declared optimizer ownership. It cannot substitute for START's reconstructed-map input, transformer fusion, VAE, explicit supervised estimates, or PPO training. Freezing the old actor permanently would materially constrain the graft. [supplied design §3; START §§II-A–II-C]
7. Learn from scratch: depth CNN, reconstruction GRU, rough decoder, refinement U-Net, map CNN, transformer fusion, VAE heads/decoder, explicit estimate heads/decoders, and new actor-conditioning parameters unless an inspected compatible pretrained module exists. The E1 0.2-second proprioceptive student has not thereby learned camera geometry, occluded local mapping, or edge-aware sparse-foot placement. Fine-tune compatible existing MoE actor/gating and critic parameters for Go2 sparse terrain; keep the old student only where its input/latent semantics remain valid. A new proprioceptive GRU is required unless compatibility with an existing recurrent representation is established. [supplied design §§0,3; START §§II-A,II-B]
8. Training: use concurrent PPO, estimator supervision, and reconstruction supervision with AdaSmpl. Use ground truth only in critic/auxiliary targets and probabilistic training-map substitution. Keep reconstruction active throughout training and deploy with reconstructed maps only. Any warm-start diagnostic phase is an engineering addition; a separate privileged-policy training then vision distillation pipeline would depart from START's reported single-stage method. Record all invented hyperparameters and gradient boundaries. [START §§II-A–II-D]
9. Rewards and terrain: implement all 14 Table I terms and Eq. (6), the four terrain families, 10-level difficulty, two-level stone randomization, low-to-high terrain progression, and gap-specific difficulty handling. Retaining additional E1 rewards, air-time reward, feet-center reward, or old terrain mixtures creates additional experimental factors and must be reported. A faithful-recipe branch should preserve START's reported geometry first; Go2-scaled geometry can be a separately identified adaptation. Paper thresholds that are absent must be chosen explicitly. [START §II-D; supplied design §§3–4]
10. Budget and deployment: use the Lite3 budget as a reference only. Measure Go2 environment throughput and memory before choosing parallelism or forecasting time. Target D435i depth at 10 Hz and actor targets at 50 Hz, while defining reconstruction cadence, frame spacing, recurrent resets, latency handling, and held-map behavior. Orin NX/TensorRT deployment is the paper reference; the actual Go2 compute target is unspecified. [START §§II-D.1,III-C]
11. Proposed evaluation: retain E1 and the supplied registered base-locomotion evaluation, then compare the full hybrid with HMap GT and all seven non-GT ablations under matched Go2 conditions. Measure complete-traversal success, distance fraction, contact-gated edge violations, reconstruction errors including edge/occluded regions, reward learning curves, gait preservation, and deployment latency. Reproduce reported 6 m/500-run simulation and five-trial lab protocols where practical, while distinguishing the project's additional statistical protocol. Exact simulation-plot benchmarks cannot be reconstructed from this text. No evaluation or equivalence claim is made here. [START §III; supplied design §§5–6]
